lines.text: My brother rode into the Lists on a white warhorse, in black and gold, with the Order's ribbon on his arm. He looked exactly like the hero of a song. He always had.
The court adored it. A Varr heir with five rings, fighting for the Order against the zero's peasants. It was the best story of the winter.
I went down to the champions' enclosure before his first bout. Captain Holt let me. I think he felt sorry for me.
Maric. That's the Order's draught in you. I can see it under your skin. It nearly killed you once.
It nearly made me what I was born to be. Go back to your box, little brother. Watch.
In the veins of his wrists, something burned white. Like milk with a lamp behind it.
His first opponent was a knight of four rings. The bout lasted as long as it took the herald to finish shouting.
White fire. Not the red Ember of House Varr. White, and silent, and so hot that the sand under his feet turned to glass.
His second opponent yielded before Maric reached him. The nobles laughed and cheered. The Lowmarket said nothing at all.
Wren's bout was against the Princess herself. Mirelle got her rematch in front of the whole city. She lost it by a hair, and laughed out loud.
Caddoc won his bout loudly. His opponent was carried off the sand, and didn't move on the way.
That evening, the heralds drew the last four. Oswin. Wren. Caddoc. And Maric.
Oswin would fight my brother first.
That's the draught, my lord. White as milk. I saw vials of it in the College infirmary. The Measurers who drank it stopped coming to lectures.
I beat him once, at Senn Ford. He's been waiting a year for this.
You beat him with a hangover.
I had a hangover every day that year. That's not the point.
Late that night, I went to find Maric one more time. He was alone in the stables, sitting in the straw.
His hands were shaking. Where they rested on his knees, the straw had begun to smoke.
Let me help you. A bond. You only have to say yes.
And glow like one of your peasants, because the zero feels sorry for me? I would rather burn.
He coughed. A little white fire came out with it, and drifted up into the dark like sparks from a forge.
Tomorrow I beat the drunk who shamed me. Then Caddoc. And then everyone will remember which of us is the Varr.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-nine, coming soon.
